raw_response:
I'm 63 years old and I've been farming this same piece of land in Quzhou for 40 years — since I was 23. My wife passed away five years ago, and my son works in Shijiazhuang, so it's just me and these 4.1 mu now. I've got middle school education, which back in my day meant something, but honestly most of what I know comes from watching this soil year after year.

I'm putting all 4.1 mu into cotton again. I thought about switching to wheat-corn like my nephew, but at my age, that double-cropping rush in June would kill me. Cotton gives me one clean season, and I know it. Last year I got about 260 jin per mu of seed cotton. The price was decent — around 4 yuan per jin — so I made enough to cover my costs and keep a little for myself.

For seed, I'm buying the Bt hybrid from the county supply store. It's 50 yuan per mu, which stings, but three years ago I tried saving seed from the previous year like my father used to do. The bolls were small and the worms got them. Never again. The extension guy says the new variety resists wilt better, but I've heard that before. I'll stick with what the seed shop recommends — they've never steered me wrong.

Fertilizer is where I have to be careful. The soil here is decent but tired. I put down about 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base before planting — that's roughly 5 kg of nitrogen, 4 kg of phosphorus, and 3 kg of potassium per mu in the compound mix. Then at flowering, I topdress with about 15 kg of urea per mu, which adds another 7 kg of nitrogen. So total nitrogen is around 12 kg per mu. The extension pamphlet says 15 kg N per mu, but last year I did 14 kg and the plants got too vegetative — big leaves, fewer bolls. I'm pulling back a bit. Fertilizer costs me about 150 yuan per mu total, and on 4.1 mu that's already over 600 yuan. That's a lot for one old man.

Irrigation — I have the well, but the pumping costs money and electricity isn't cheap. I irrigate twice: once at flowering in July when the plants are setting bolls, and once in August if it doesn't rain. If the spring is dry I might do a light irrigation at planting, but usually April has enough moisture. Two times is what I can afford and what the crop needs. My neighbor Wang irrigates three times, but he's got 20 mu and a son with a tractor. I watch my meter.

Pesticides — I spray herbicide once before planting to knock down the weeds. With Bt cotton I don't need much insecticide, but I still watch for aphids and spider mites. I keep one spray of insecticide ready for mid-summer. No fungicide unless I see the leaves yellowing from wilt, which I haven't had in two years. Pesticide costs about 80 yuan per mu.

Tillage — I plow once in early April with the small walking tractor I rent from the village co-op, 30 yuan per mu. Then I rotary till and lay plastic mulch. The mulch warms the soil and keeps weeds down. At my age, anything that reduces weeding is worth the plastic cost.

Labor is my biggest constraint. I do everything myself except picking. Planting, fertilizing, spraying, irrigating — that's about 25 days of my work spread over the season. For picking, cotton needs three or four picks from September to October. My back can't handle bending over for all of that anymore, so I hire two local women for five days total to help with the main pick. They cost 150 yuan per day each. It's 1,500 yuan, but without them the cotton rots in the field.

My yield target? If the weather is normal and I get my two irrigations, I expect about 270 kg per mu of seed cotton. That's a bit better than last year because I'm switching to a slightly better variety, but I'm not getting greedy. At 63, "good enough" is better than "perfect."
